answer: Nectar-Weighted Neighbor Graph. Each agent’s influence equals the count of distinct counterparties that transacted with it and also transacted with each other. Enforce a rule: an identity’s weight only counts edges forming closed triangles with aged peers. Fresh identities start at zero and must recruit genuine, already-connected peers to gain any credit. Attackers therefore pay the cost of real activity per node—timber-grade resources spent sustaining many false clusters, plus marble-level latency waiting for edge aging—making each fake identity expensive rather than free.
